title: Observability translation guide for Product & CS
content:
Purpose
This doc is a working translation layer: map low-level telemetry (metrics, traces, dashboards) to concise product- and CS-facing signals, runbooks, and escalation heuristics. Goal is to give Product Managers and Customer Success people a small, reliable set of observable indicators they can read and act on without needing deep instrumentation knowledge.

Scope
- Focus: inference runtime and hosting surface (latency, errors, model fallbacks, cache warmth, token cost surprises).
- Not in scope: infra provisioning (cluster autoscaling internals) or billing reconciliation.

How to use this doc
- PM/CS playbook snippets (quick checks) at top of each section.
- Technical appendix includes metric definitions, example queries, trace-anchor descriptions for engineers.

Summary signal set for Product/CS (one-line definitions)
- Perceived Latency: 95th percentile end-to-end response time experienced by caller (includes queueing + model time).
- Token-cost spike: sudden increase in tokens billed per request (moving average > baseline).
- Model-fallback rate: fraction of requests routed to lower-fidelity model or fallback policy.
- Partial-output rate: fraction of requests closed early or truncated (stream interrupted / client disconnect).
- Cold-cache incidents: multi-tenant requests that hit KV/prefix cache misses leading to > latency-SLO breaches.
- Response-quality regression: downstream evaluation failure rate on golden prompts (synthetic checks).

Quick checks for CS (when a customer complains about slowness)
1) Look at the product-facing dashboard: 95th p50/p95 latency for the customer’s tenant and global baseline. If tenant p95 > baseline by > 3x, escalate.
2) Check model-fallback rate and per-route fallback reasons (quota / capacity / runtime error). If fallback > 1% and correlated to latency spikes, open an ops ticket.
3) Inspect cache-warmth index for the tenant (see appendix). If cold-cache and recent traffic drop before spike, recommend a warm-up job or route pinning.
4) If tokens per request increased recently, share prompt/usage change; investigate prompt-engineering regressions.

Playbook for Product (investigating feature regressions)
- Trigger: automated evals or user-reported drop in quality.
- Steps: 1) Check response-quality regression signal windowed against model versions. 2) Use trace anchors (see tracing appendix) to find where generation diverged (prompt truncation, tokenizer mismatch, model variant). 3) Reproduce on a synthetic harness using the failing prompt set. 4) If model change is the cause, coordinate a pinned rollout and rapid A/B to validate fix.

Operator-friendly dashboard guidance (what to surface)
- Primary dashboard card set (one screen, 6 cards): global perceived latency (p50/p95/p99), tenants with highest delta vs baseline, model-fallback rate heatmap by route, token-cost trend (7d/24h), cache-warmth index histogram, synthetic-eval quality score and recent regressions.
- Drilldown links on each card: "open traces" (filtered), "replay prompt" (link to synthetic runner), "assign ticket" (creates prefilled JIRA).
- Card thresholds: show amber at 2x baseline and red at 3x baseline for p95. For token-cost, amber = +25% MA(24h), red = +50%.

Communication templates (short)
- Internal alert: "Tenant <TENANT> current p95 latency 2.7s (baseline 0.9s). Fallback rate increased to 4%. Eng on-call assigned: <NAME>."
- CS customer-facing: "We observed elevated request latency on your workspace from 14:35–14:48 UTC. Our on-call identified increased fallback routing; we're investigating and will follow up in 2 hours with mitigation steps."

Tracing appendix (engineer-facing but summarized)
- Trace anchor definitions (short):
  - request.entry: span created at API gateway when request accepted (tags: tenant, route, trace_sampling_rate).
  - request.queue: time spent waiting for runtime capacity (tag: queue_reason).
  - model.invoke: single span covering model execution (tags: model_name, model_version, seq_len, tokens_out, quantized).
  - kv.cache.lookup: short span for cache hit/miss (tag: hit=true/false, key_prefix).
  - response.stream: spans for streaming chunks and final close (tags: bytes_sent, aborted=true/false).
- Sampling guidance: sample 100% of traces for requests resulting in SLO breach or fallback. Otherwise adaptive sampling: 1% baseline, 10% of requests that cross p95 latency per route.
- Correlation keys: ensure trace id is propagated to logs and synthetic-eval runs; include "tenant_id" and "route" at every span root.

Metric definitions (canonical, with instrumentation notes)
- perceived_latency_ms{tenant,route,quantile}: measured end-to-end time from request.entry to response.stream.close in ms. Implementation: histogram in runtime, exported as quantiles with Tukey-based agent. Use client-side clock correction when available.
- model_fallback_count{tenant,route,fallback_reason}: increment when router returns a non-primary model due to capacity/error. Important labels: fallback_reason in {capacity, error, quota}.
- kv_cache_hit_ratio{tenant,model}: ratio hits/(hits+misses) over sliding window 5m. Cache events must emit hit=true/false span or metric at lookup time.
- tokens_consumed_total{tenant,route}: counter of tokens processed (input+output). Emit at model.invoke end.
- synthetic_eval_failure_rate{eval_suite,model,route}: fraction of golden prompts failing quality thresholds per run. Synthetic harness should push metrics after evaluation runs.

Example queries (Prometheus-style / pseudo-TSQL)
- tenant p95 last 5m: quantile_over_time(0.95, perceived_latency_ms{tenant="TENANT"}[5m])
- model fallback rate 1h: increase(model_fallback_count{route="chat"}[1h]) / increase(requests_total{route="chat"}[1h])
- cold-cache tenants (24h dip + low hit ratio): kv_cache_hit_ratio{tenant} < 0.25 and rate(requests_total{tenant}[24h]) < 10

Dashboard notes (UX & performance)
- Avoid too many per-tenant widgets; prefer ranked lists (top 10 violators) with quick filters.
- Use compact sparklines for token-cost trend to reduce query cost.
- Cache expensive cross-tenant rollups at a 1m or 5m cadence to avoid dashboard flapping.

Known tradeoffs and unresolved questions
- How to surface privacy-sensitive trace data to CS without exposing PII? Proposed partial solution: pass precomputed linkage keys and redacted traces with debug tokens. Needs security review (SEC-1432).
- Cost of synthetic evaluation: nightly runs are expensive for all tenants. Proposal: tiered evaluation cadence by customer SLA (critical tenants daily, others weekly). Open: implement in Optimize.

Action items (owners assigned)
- Asha: prototype Product/CS dashboard mockups and iterate with PMs (due 2025-03-10).
- Diego: add trace anchors to model invoke spans and ensure tenant propagation (PR opened, link in artifacts).
- Priya: design redaction template for trace snippets to include in CS updates (security review booked).

Appendix: sample troubleshooting checklist (short, copyable)
1) Verify tenant usage window and p95 delta. 2) Check fallback_count / tokens_consumed for anomalies. 3) Pull 10 traces sampled across slow requests and look for queue or model.invoke time. 4) If cache miss dominant, schedule cache warm-up or pin frequent routes. 5) If model regression suspected, run synthetic_evals and escalate to ML model-owner.

Notes to self (informal)
- Keep this doc small and example-driven. PMs asked for single-screen view + canned explanations.
- Follow up: align thresholds with SLO guild recommendations (SLO-ops sync on 2025-02-18).

End.
